title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The section is about the 'équation des lacets' (loop equation). Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free profinite on the loops l_0 and l_1. ρ is the order-3 automorphism coming from the cyclic permutation of the three points, with ρ(l_0) = l_1. σ_∞ is the involution fixing ∞ and exchanging 0 and 1, with σ_∞(l_0) = l_1. τ_∞ is an orientation-reversing involution of the complex-conjugation type, and Π̃ = Π̂_{0,3}·{1, τ_∞}. The unknown is an automorphism u of Π̂_{0,3} that is compatible, up to inner automorphisms, with this S_3-type symmetry and acts on the inertia at 0 by u(l_0) = int(f^{-1})(l_0^μ), where μ = 2ν+1. This is the pair (λ, f) of the later Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, with λ = μ and m = (λ−1)/2 = ν. Grothendieck rewrites the 2-cycle and 3-cycle conditions in non-abelian cohomological form. The 3-cycle condition becomes ψ·ρ(ψ)·ρ²(ψ) = 1 with ψ = f·ρ(f)^{-1}; this is equation (24), with ξ its companion. The 2-cycle condition becomes η·σ_∞(η) = 1, with φ as companion. Compatibility relations (19) and (23) tie the pairs together.

Previous page. If the solution ψ is parametrised by an f lying in the nontrivial coset τ_∞Π̂_{0,3}, the construction still makes sense.

Remark 1 (end), this page. Write f = τ_∞ f_0. Then u(l_0) = int(f_0^{-1})(τ_∞(l_0^μ)) = int(f_0^{-1})(l_0^{-μ}). So u is again a 'local' automorphism, now of multiplier −μ. The Z/2 obstruction (the class of f in Π̃/Π̂ ≅ Z/2) records the sign of the multiplier, i.e. the complex-conjugation component.

Remark 2. For fixed g and h, f is determined only up to f ↦ l_0^n f with n in Ẑ (25). This is the centralizer of l_0 in the free profinite group, the closure of ⟨l_0⟩. The induced substitutions are as follows.
- ψ' = l_0^n ψ l_1^{-n}: the ρ-twisted conjugate by l_0^{±n}, since ρ(l_0) = l_1.
- φ, ξ, η transform similarly; ξ is ρ-twisted and φ, η are σ_∞-twisted.
- In the margin: α_0 ↦ l_0^n α_0 and β_0 ↦ l_0^{±n} β_0 (26). These are the 'trivialisers' introduced on the next page.
Because these are twisted conjugations by an element of the centralizer of l_0, the cocycle equations (16) and (24) and the compatibilities (19) and (23) are invariant. This makes the indeterminacy harmless; it is the ambiguity that Drinfeld/Ihara later kill by requiring f to lie in the (closure of the) commutator subgroup.

Remark 3. Equation (11) is rewritten as (27):
σ_∞(h)·g = (l_0^ν f)^{-1} ξ ρ(l_0^ν f) = σ_∞(f^{-1}l_0^ν) η (f^{-1}l_0^ν)^{-1}.
The same element σ_∞(h)g is therefore both a ρ-twisted conjugate of ξ and a σ_∞-twisted conjugate of η.
- For h = 1, the first form is the useful one; it yields the equation in ξ.
- For g = 1, apply σ_∞ to the second form and use σ_∞(η) = η^{-1}. This gives (28): h = (f^{-1}l_0^ν) η^{-1} σ_∞(f^{-1}l_0^ν)^{-1}, i.e. h is the σ_∞-transform of η^{-1}.
On the next page this is used to relate the trivialisations g = αρ(α)^{-1} and ξ = α_0ρ(α_0)^{-1}, and likewise h = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} and η = β_0σ_∞(β_0)^{-1}.

Purpose. To parametrise and normalise the solutions of the loop equation, i.e. the (λ, f) pairs, by non-abelian Z/3- and Z/2-cohomology classes in Π̂_{0,3}, and to keep track of the residual ambiguity coming from the tangential base point at 0.
errors: As transcribed, ξ' = l_0^{-n} ξ l_1^{-n} and η' = l_0^{-n} η l_1^{-n} are not twisted conjugations. With these formulas the equations ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 (or its analogue) and ησ_∞(η) = 1 would NOT be invariant, so the stated invariance fails.

Deriving the substitutions from (27) with g, h fixed gives ξ' = l_0^n ξ l_1^{-n} (same shape as ψ') and η' = l_1^n η l_0^{-n}. These do preserve η·σ_∞(η) = 1 and the telescoping 3-cycle product. The exponents/sides on the page are either misread or a slip by Grothendieck.
The NB says ψ', ξ' are 'ρ-transformés par l_0^{-n}'. This is consistent only with the convention x ↦ a^{-1}·x·ρ(a), so the conventions are implicit and slightly unstable across the page.
(28) itself checks out: apply σ_∞ to (27) with g = 1 and use σ_∞(η) = η^{-1}.

ideas.what: Rewriting the 3-cycle and 2-cycle relations for (λ, f) as non-abelian cocycle equations ψρ(ψ)ρ²(ψ) = 1 and ησ_∞(η) = 1. Solutions are parametrised as coboundaries ψ = fρ(f)^{-1}, with a Z/2 obstruction (the coset of τ_∞).
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon/2-cycle relations of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, viewed as non-abelian H^1 of Z/3 and Z/2 acting on F̂_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990-91); cohomological reformulations in Lochak–Schneps and Schneps' surveys
ideas.where_published: Spirit only: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the role of P^1 minus 3 points and the 'Teichmüller tower' relations; the detailed equations are in the unpublished Longue Marche notes

ideas.what: If f lies in the τ_∞ coset, u is an automorphism with multiplier −μ, i.e. the orientation-reversing / complex-conjugation component.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of GT-type automorphisms to include λ of the 'conjugation' type
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in GT literature (complex conjugation corresponds to λ = −1, f = 1)

ideas.what: The indeterminacy f ↦ l_0^n f by the centralizer of l_0, with the induced twisted conjugations of all auxiliary cocycles and the invariance of the equations.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential-base-point ambiguity; normalisation f ∈ [F̂_2, F̂_2]^ in GT

ideas.what: A single element σ_∞(h)g expressed simultaneously as a ρ-twisted conjugate of ξ and a σ_∞-twisted conjugate of η.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility between Z/3- and Z/2-trivialisations (S_3-equivariance of the GT data)

missed.claim: This is a pre-Drinfeld (c. 1981-82) derivation of the 2- and 3-cycle relations of what became the profinite GT group. It is written in an explicitly non-abelian-cohomological (twisted cocycle/coboundary) form, with careful bookkeeping of the l_0^n ambiguity and the Z/2 conjugation obstruction. It documents Grothendieck's independent route to GT relations, but the content of this page is routine bookkeeping.
missed.quote: l'indétermination de f (quand on fixe g, h fixés) est donc f ↦ f' = l_0^n f (n ∈ Ẑ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: History and priority of the GT relations; the cocycle formulation may be pedagogically useful. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: These are consistent but routine manipulations (indeterminacy, invariance, rewriting of (11)) within Grothendieck's known unpublished pre-GT work. The historical interest lies in the section as a whole, not in anything new on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'u est un automorphisme : locale, de multiplication −μ' should probably read 'u est un automorphisme "local", de multiplicateur −μ = −(2ν+1)'.
Margin NB likely reads: 'on a de même α_0 ↦ α_0' = l_0^n α_0, β_0 ↦ β_0' = l_0^{−n} β_0 (26)'; the transcription has β_0' = l_0^n.

In the first line of the substitutions the exponent of l_1 on ψ' is hard to read; it should be l_1^{-n}. The ξ', η' lines as transcribed are mathematically inconsistent with the claimed invariance (see errors).
'(16) (en φ et en ξ)' is as transcribed; the compatibility reference may be '(19)' or '(14)', which is unclear in the image.
